hypothesis: The worker pacing of the runtime design (200 µs burst, in-step waits of up to 50 µs in start, stop and power sequencing, a single worker wait with a 4 ms bound while a job is in flight, a 1 ms CPU-run bound) meets the design's budgets in the host models.
prediction: Budgets of the design (target column): worker timed wake-ups per second with a job running 250 without qualified SPI 63 and 0 after; worker ticks from unpark to first kick 0 when every wait ends within 50 µs (1 wake-up); park to STOPPED 0 (1 wake-up); ticks from send to kick 0 (at most one context switch); client wake-ups per compute job 2 (baseline 1 per tick + 32); the other rows of the design budget table are listed in the design document.

conditions.no_board: all values come from host models in QEMU or on the host
conditions.method: each commit exported with git archive and built under ~/.cache/sunstoneos/build/gpu-runtime-measure/; checks/pvr-gpu-service.py cases 1-3 of the service model and cases 1, 5, 6 of the asynchronous power model in QEMU; checks/pvr-compute-service.py cases 1-11 and 15-21, with case 7 of the base harness given the same 50-tick job window; checks/a733-gpu-power.c compiled for the host with a counter in the first power-on and power-off poll loop; llvm-objdump, llvm-size and llvm-nm on the sunstone-a733-gpu-render image

conclusion: Of the design, only worker pacing is implemented at the measured commit: the 200 µs burst, in-step waits of up to 50 µs, the single worker wait with a 4 ms bound while a job is in flight, and the 1 ms CPU-run bound. All values come from host models, no board. Models answer every hardware wait at once, so tick figures measure pacing overhead, not GPU time. Results (base commit c45a76e vs measured commit 9a010a6): worker timed wake-ups during a job without interrupt delivery 50 in 50 ticks (1,000 per second) to 12 in 50 ticks (240 per second), target 250 per second without qualified SPI 63, met; ready and idle without interrupt callbacks 200 in 200 ticks to 4 in 200 ticks (interim until park); ticks from OPEN reply to READY with synchronous power 5 to 2 with 0 timed waits; with the power controller 34 to 2 with 0 timed waits; CLOSE reply to STOPPED with the power controller 10 to 1 with 0 timed waits; power controller polls power-on and power-off 32 and 11 to 1 and 1; power controller callbacks for the first power-on 91 to 62; ticks from compute OPEN to READY 13 to 14 to 10 to 13 with 0 timed waits; timed waits or tick blocks from compute admission to kick not countable at base, 0 at every kick (target 0, met); scheduler ticks from compute admission to kick 3 at both commits (target at most one context switch); ticks from fence write to COMPLETE with no client requests 1 to 2 (within the 4 ms bound without interrupt delivery); longest CPU run outside ring writes before a kick 1,201 to 1,775 µs against the 1 ms bound checked after each burst; tick blocks per compute case 5 to 6, all during OPEN. Admission to kick took 2,854 to 3,125 µs of emulator time in the current compute model across three scheduler ticks at both commits; the current worker spends that time computing with no timed wait or tick block, and the base harness has no counter to separate CPU time from waits. The CPU-run bound is checked between steps after each burst, so a run can exceed 1 ms by one 200 µs burst, its last step and the time that tasks of the worker's priority use after each yield. Completion without interrupt delivery takes up to 4 ms instead of one tick, which trades 1,000 fewer timed wake-ups per second at PVR_GPU_SERVICE_JOB_POLL_US and is removed once SPI 63 delivery is qualified on the board. Budget rows not implemented keep their baseline at both commits (no barrier, cache maintenance, copy or translation code changed; the render image of each commit contains 303 DSB, 9 DMB, 132 ISB, 4 DC, 2 AT instructions and 220 memcpy calls): jobs in flight 1 (target render 1 + compute 2); client wake-ups per compute job 1 per tick + 32 (2); DC lines per park and unpark 2,176 + 2,176 (2,176 + 0); queue round trips for a 3,968-byte result 31 (0 beyond completion); copies per input byte and per result byte 2 and at least 5 (0 for EL1 clients, 1 for EL0); copies per rendered frame byte 2 (0 for scanout); compute job cache work 132 or 192 lines and a 256- or 4,096-byte fill (written input / 64 + read output / 64, no fill); DSB SY per submit and per FWCCB drain 16 transport + 2 per cache call and 11n + 5 (5 and 2); AT per register read 5 (0); GPU MMU leaf entries for a 4 MiB buffer 1,024 (2); hang detection none (max_job_us + 4 ms); firmware header decodes 1 per call at 5 sites (1 per boot); firmware hashes 0 (1 per boot + 1 per reset). Unpark wall-clock time and the free-extent check need the board or park and are not measured. Image size, render image text 462,640 B to 464,236 B (+1,596), bss 823,153,872 B to 823,154,000 B (+128), gpu-service-model text 280,376 B to 283,384 B (+3,008), gpu-compute-service-model text 318,316 B to 321,612 B (+3,296); in the render image the worker grows by 612 bytes, a733_gpu_power_poll by 376, pvr_gpu_start_poll by 312 and pvr_gpu_stop_poll by 280, holding the in-step clock waits, the time-bounded burst and the pacing counters; the bss growth is those counters.
narrative: Logs, harness copies and executable hashes are in ~/.cache/sunstoneos/build/gpu-runtime-measure/runs/. The base harness received only the observation code of the current harness (a count of scheduler ticks with at least one worker callback and a phase observer that sends no requests); in the base worker every wait lasts one tick, so ticks with worker activity equal its timed wake-ups. A further copy of both compute harnesses recorded the scheduler tick at each admission of a COMPUTE or COMPUTE_INPUT request and the tick at its kick.
